top_news.title: Seven vie for three Haywood commission seats -
top_news.summary: Three of five Haywood County commission seats are up for election this year, and at least two will be filled by newcomers. The county has seen its fair share of hardship over the last several years, beginning with the COVID-19 pandemic that gripped the country beginning in 2020. In August 2021, Tropical Storm Fred caused widespread property damage and littered debris in waterways. The largest employer, Pactiv Evergreen, shut down its Canton paper mill, almost instantly eliminating over a thousand jobs. Most recently, in September 2024, Haywood was one of a dozen or so counties to bear the brunt of Hurricane Helene’s wrath, which caused about $60 billion in total damage in North Carolina.

top_news.title: India calls for cessation of attacks on civilian infra in Saudi Arabia after death of national; reaffirms committment towards welfare of diaspora
top_news.summary: India on Wednesday expressed stern condemnation of the recent attacks on civilian infrastructure in Saudi Arabia and called for immediate cessation, while reaffirming its resolve to ensure the safety and welfare of nationals abroad after an Indian died in a Houthi attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh. During a bi-weekly press briefing, Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal called the ongoing attacks, including the recent one on Aramco headquarters in the region, totally unacceptable. Voicing India's solidarity with the people and government of Saudi Arabia, Jaiswal expressed hopes for restoration of peace and stability in the region. There has been a string of attacks in Saudi Arabia, including yesterday's attack on Aramco headquarters. We condemn all such attacks on civilian infrastructure and call for them to cease immediately. They are totally unacceptable. We stand in solidarity with the people and government of Saudi Arabia in defence of their sovereignty and hope for a return to peace and normalcy in the region, he said. Regarding the safety of the Indian diaspora living in Saudi Arabia, the MEA spokesperson amplified the advisory issued by the Indian Embassy in Riyadh and the updated flight schedules of Indian airlines to the region amid the airspace security crisis. Our embassy in Saudi Arabia is in regular touch with the Indian community and has issued advisories for their welfare. Flight schedules have been disrupted following attacks on airports, impacting Indian carriers, particularly flights to and from Riyadh, Dammam, Medina and Jeddah. The embassy is providing updated information to travellers and those stranded, the MEA spokesperson said. Further reflecting on the October 10 attack on Saudi Arabia's King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Jaiswal said that of the 11 Indian nationals injured, three have been discharged while eight remain under medical supervision with four in the ICU. He added that the last rites of the national who succumbed to his injuries were performed in Riyadh. He assured India's continuous support to the affected and other nationals living abroad, through the Indian Embassy. The attack on 10 October injured 12 people, one of whom unfortunately passed away. His last rites were performed in Riyadh, as wished by his family, with assistance from the embassy. Of the 11 remaining injured, three have been discharged, while eight remain hospitalised, including four in the ICU. Embassy officials are regularly visiting them and staying in touch with their families. We remain committed to doing our best for the welfare and well-being of our nationals abroad, Jaiswal stated. The death toll following a Houthi attack on Saudi Arabia's King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh has risen to 13 after the Indian Embassy in the Gulf country confirmed the death of an Indian national. India's Ambassador to Saudi Arabia, Vipul, and Embassy officials attended the funeral service of Indian national Mohammed Yousef Ali, who lost his life in the recent Houthi attack on Riyadh airport, and conveyed condolences to the bereaved family while assuring them of continued support and assistance. In an update shared on X on Sunday, the Embassy of India in Riyadh confirmed the death of the Indian national in the October 10 attack and expressed condolences to the bereaved family. Following the post, the Embassy stated that its officials had visited hospitals where the injured Indian nationals were admitted. Two other injured Indians remain hospitalised in regular wards, while the remaining injured Indian nationals have been discharged. Further Update regarding Riyadh airport attack

top_news.title: Delhi: Cabinet approves Delhi Industrial Policy 2026 under chairmanship of CM Rekha Gupta
top_news.summary: The Delhi government, under the leadership of Chief Minister Rekha Gupta, has taken a step towards developing the capital into a clean, modern and technology-driven industrial hub. According to a press release, at a Cabinet meeting chaired by the Chief Minister on Tuesday, the Delhi Industrial Policy 2026 was approved. The policy aims to promote clean, high-value industries and knowledge- and technology-based businesses over the next 10 years. It provides for an expenditure of Rs 1,000 crore on the Mukhyamantri Udyamshree Yojana over five years, from the financial year 2026-27 to 2030-31. The objective is to encourage new industries and create more employment opportunities. CM Gupta said the Delhi Industrial Policy 2026 aims to position the capital as a major hub for advanced technology, Global Capability Centres, data centres, research and development, healthcare services, urban logistics, the circular economy and advanced manufacturing. The policy will promote clean, high-value industries, attract fresh investment, modernise existing industries, encourage women entrepreneurs and expand employment opportunities for young people, the release said. She said incentives would be tailored to the needs of the 10 priority sectors, covering capital investment, office or workspace rentals, new recruitment, research, certification, technological modernisation, energy efficiency and skill development. The policy will also encourage resource reuse and waste reduction. According to the release, a 25 per cent incentive on digital infrastructure investment, up to Rs 10 crore (Rs 12 crore for women), will be available for three years. Office rental assistance of 40 per cent, up to Rs 2 crore, will also be provided for three years. Bandwidth and cloud services will qualify for 25 per cent assistance for two years, capped at Rs 10 lakh annually. An incentive of Rs 40,000 to Rs 50,000 will be provided for each new hire. A 25 per cent incentive on digital infrastructure investment, up to Rs 50 crore (Rs 60 crore for women), will be available for five years. Office rental assistance of 40 per cent, capped at Rs 2 crore, will be provided for two years. Each new hire will qualify for an incentive of Rs 1 lakh to Rs 1.2 lakh. The policy also provides 50% assistance for certification, up to Rs 25 lakh; a 30 per cent incentive for research and development, up to Rs 5 crore; and 25 per cent assistance for units developing workspaces, up to Rs 10 crore. A 25 per cent incentive on capital investment, up to Rs 10 crore (Rs 12 crore for women), will be available. The policy provides 30 per cent assistance for low-water-consumption cooling systems, capped at Rs 2 crore; 50 per cent assistance for certification and data security-related expenses, up to Rs 50 lakh; and 50 per cent assistance for regulatory compliance preparedness, up to Rs 25 lakh. The release added that a 25 per cent incentive on capital investment, up to Rs 10 crore (Rs 12 crore for women), will be available. Research activities will qualify for a 50 per cent grant, capped at Rs 50 lakh. Patent-related assistance will cover 25 per cent of the cost, up to Rs 5 lakh per patent, for a maximum of four patents. A 25 per cent incentive for laboratory accreditation-related expenses, up to Rs 25 lakh, will also be provided. A 25 per cent incentive on capital investment, generally capped at Rs 10 crore (Rs 12 crore for women), will be available. Hospitals with 1,000 or more beds will be eligible for assistance of up to Rs 100 crore. Wellness activities will qualify for a 5 per cent incentive, up to Rs 1 crore, while certification by bodies such as NABH, NABL and JCI will receive 50% assistance, capped at Rs 20 lakh. Each new appointment of a specialist doctor will qualify for an incentive of Rs 50,000 to Rs 60,000. The release said that the new warehousing units will receive a 25 per cent incentive, up to Rs 10 crore (Rs 12 crore for women), while existing units will be eligible for 25 per cent assistance, capped at Rs 1 crore. Cold-chain facilities will qualify for a 25per cent incentive, up to Rs 2 crore. Technology adoption in logistics will receive 40 per cent assistance, capped at Rs 50 lakh, while the use of green energy will qualify for a 25 per cent incentive, up to Rs 2 crore. articles.summary: Three of five Haywood County commission seats are up for election this year, and at least two will be filled by newcomers. The county has seen its fair share of hardship over the last several years, beginning with the COVID-19 pandemic that gripped the country beginning in 2020. In August 2021, Tropical Storm Fred caused widespread property damage and littered debris in waterways. The largest employer, Pactiv Evergreen, shut down its Canton paper mill, almost instantly eliminating over a thousand jobs. Most recently, in September 2024, Haywood was one of a dozen or so counties to bear the brunt of Hurricane Helene’s wrath, which caused about $60 billion in total damage in North Carolina.

articles.title: India calls for cessation of attacks on civilian infra in Saudi Arabia after death of national; reaffirms committment towards welfare of diaspora
articles.summary: India on Wednesday expressed stern condemnation of the recent attacks on civilian infrastructure in Saudi Arabia and called for immediate cessation, while reaffirming its resolve to ensure the safety and welfare of nationals abroad after an Indian died in a Houthi attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh. During a bi-weekly press briefing, Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal called the ongoing attacks, including the recent one on Aramco headquarters in the region, totally unacceptable. Voicing India's solidarity with the people and government of Saudi Arabia, Jaiswal expressed hopes for restoration of peace and stability in the region. There has been a string of attacks in Saudi Arabia, including yesterday's attack on Aramco headquarters. We condemn all such attacks on civilian infrastructure and call for them to cease immediately. They are totally unacceptable. We stand in solidarity with the people and government of Saudi Arabia in defence of their sovereignty and hope for a return to peace and normalcy in the region, he said. Regarding the safety of the Indian diaspora living in Saudi Arabia, the MEA spokesperson amplified the advisory issued by the Indian Embassy in Riyadh and the updated flight schedules of Indian airlines to the region amid the airspace security crisis. Our embassy in Saudi Arabia is in regular touch with the Indian community and has issued advisories for their welfare. Flight schedules have been disrupted following attacks on airports, impacting Indian carriers, particularly flights to and from Riyadh, Dammam, Medina and Jeddah. The embassy is providing updated information to travellers and those stranded, the MEA spokesperson said. articles.title: Delhi: Cabinet approves Delhi Industrial Policy 2026 under chairmanship of CM Rekha Gupta
articles.summary: The Delhi government, under the leadership of Chief Minister Rekha Gupta, has taken a step towards developing the capital into a clean, modern and technology-driven industrial hub. According to a press release, at a Cabinet meeting chaired by the Chief Minister on Tuesday, the Delhi Industrial Policy 2026 was approved. The policy aims to promote clean, high-value industries and knowledge- and technology-based businesses over the next 10 years. It provides for an expenditure of Rs 1,000 crore on the Mukhyamantri Udyamshree Yojana over five years, from the financial year 2026-27 to 2030-31. The objective is to encourage new industries and create more employment opportunities. CM Gupta said the Delhi Industrial Policy 2026 aims to position the capital as a major hub for advanced technology, Global Capability Centres, data centres, research and development, healthcare services, urban logistics, the circular economy and advanced manufacturing. The policy will promote clean, high-value industries, attract fresh investment, modernise existing industries, encourage women entrepreneurs and expand employment opportunities for young people, the release said. She said incentives would be tailored to the needs of the 10 priority sectors, covering capital investment, office or workspace rentals, new recruitment, research, certification, technological modernisation, energy efficiency and skill development. The policy will also encourage resource reuse and waste reduction. According to the release, a 25 per cent incentive on digital infrastructure investment, up to Rs 10 crore (Rs 12 crore for women), will be available for three years. Office rental assistance of 40 per cent, up to Rs 2 crore, will also be provided for three years. Bandwidth and cloud services will qualify for 25 per cent assistance for two years, capped at Rs 10 lakh annually. An incentive of Rs 40,000 to Rs 50,000 will be provided for each new hire. A 25 per cent incentive on digital infrastructure investment, up to Rs 50 crore (Rs 60 crore for women), will be available for five years. Office rental assistance of 40 per cent, capped at Rs 2 crore, will be provided for two years. Each new hire will qualify for an incentive of Rs 1 lakh to Rs 1.2 lakh. The policy also provides 50% assistance for certification, up to Rs 25 lakh; a 30 per cent incentive for research and development, up to Rs 5 crore; and 25 per cent assistance for units developing workspaces, up to Rs 10 crore. A 25 per cent incentive on capital investment, up to Rs 10 crore (Rs 12 crore for women), will be available. The policy provides 30 per cent assistance for low-water-consumption cooling systems, capped at Rs 2 crore; 50 per cent assistance for certification and data security-related expenses, up to Rs 50 lakh; and 50 per cent assistance for regulatory compliance preparedness, up to Rs 25 lakh. The release added that a 25 per cent incentive on capital investment, up to Rs 10 crore (Rs 12 crore for women), will be available. Research activities will qualify for a 50 per cent grant, capped at Rs 50 lakh. Patent-related assistance will cover 25 per cent of the cost, up to Rs 5 lakh per patent, for a maximum of four patents. A 25 per cent incentive for laboratory accreditation-related expenses, up to Rs 25 lakh, will also be provided. A 25 per cent incentive on capital investment, generally capped at Rs 10 crore (Rs 12 crore for women), will be available. Hospitals with 1,000 or more beds will be eligible for assistance of up to Rs 100 crore. Wellness activities will qualify for a 5 per cent incentive, up to Rs 1 crore, while certification by bodies such as NABH, NABL and JCI will receive 50% assistance, capped at Rs 20 lakh. Each new appointment of a specialist doctor will qualify for an incentive of Rs 50,000 to Rs 60,000. The release said that the new warehousing units will receive a 25 per cent incentive, up to Rs 10 crore (Rs 12 crore for women), while existing units will be eligible for 25 per cent assistance, capped at Rs 1 crore. Cold-chain facilities will qualify for a 25per cent incentive, up to Rs 2 crore. Technology adoption in logistics will receive 40 per cent assistance, capped at Rs 50 lakh, while the use of green energy will qualify for a 25 per cent incentive, up to Rs 2 crore.
